items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: I was just talking with a friend of mine earlier today about this, a trumpeter named Pharez Whitted.

ctx.x: Yeah. And even some of the middle-aged jazz artists I guess I would say, who have record labels, most of them are not happy with their record labels.

Correct. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. I was just talking with a friend of mine earlier today about this, a trumpeter named Pharez Whitted. And he recently took his project to a company called Origin Records, where he can — I think you pay them a fee of about four or five thousand dollars and they’ll package your product and so you get good artwork in the packaging; they will do the publicity and the radio promo for a good maybe four to six week run, maybe an eight week run of promo; and they have international ©…

distribution. All for four or five grand. And those — you pay more than that, a record company, because they don’t have all that in-house so they will pay more than that for all those services. So that’s a pretty good deal. So there are ways of doing this without going the traditional route of sending in your CD to a record label with the promo kit and everything — will you sign me? So, yeah.
